name: Action Construction Equipment Ltd
title: Action Construction Equipment Ltd - 532762 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 total income rose 15% QoQ to INR1,021 crore, but FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.33%; management plans 9-10% price hikes to offset 11-14% cost inflation.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the company's best ever revenue quarter, with total income of INR1,021 crore (up 15% QoQ, 5.58% YoY) and EBITDA of INR163.7 crore (16% margin). FY26 total income was flat at about INR3,395 crore, with EBITDA up about 4% to INR622 crore and PAT up 5.4% to INR425 crore. Other income was negative in Q4 on mark-to-market losses on surplus-cash investments, and March brought West Asia-driven steel and crude cost inflation. Management is taking staged price increases and has withheld annual guidance until the middle of Q2.

segments.name: Cranes, metal handling and construction equipment
segments.commentary: FY26 income over INR2,946 crore with an 18.6% margin and INR548 crore profit; management called FY26 a normalisation year after the pre-buying ahead of the emission transition in FY25.

segments.name: Agri division
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9% to around INR251 crore in FY26, with margins at about 1%.

segments.name: Others (miscellaneous exports)
segments.commentary: Separately reported line of about INR76.55 crore; management said it is mainly miscellaneous exports, including some construction equipment, and no volume figure is available.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: management expects growth of 15-20% or slightly more, helped by a low base in Q1 FY26; no full-year guidance given until the middle of Q2.
Pricing: 1-1.5% hike in January, about 4% from 1 May, and a further 5% from 1 June (total 9-10%); management sees total cost inflation of 11-14% and may take another 3-4% later in Q2.
Margins: target EBITDA ex-other income of 15-16%; management said expanding margins beyond about 17-18% including other income would hurt market share.
Other income expected to recover to INR20-35 crore in Q1 FY27 if markets hold or improve, after partial April recovery of March mark-to-market losses.
Defense: execution of about INR200-220 crore in FY27 (5-6% of revenue vs about 3% last year); about INR575 crore order book; rough terrain forklift/telehandler execution to start next quarter.

Long-term: INR6,000-6,200 crore revenue target by FY29 (worst case FY30) implies adding about INR700-800 crore a year; exports plus defense targeted at 10-15% of the segment, with about 11-13% expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation for cranes, metal handling and construction equipment is about 60%.

FY27 capex about INR200 crore: about INR130-135 crore for a land parcel contracted about 1-1.5 years ago, INR40-50 crore for a new defense and new-product plant within the existing complex, and INR20-25 crore maintenance.

Proposed new tower crane factory with capex upwards of INR400 crore; 12-18 months to build; decision to start this year is need-based, and management expects only about INR150 crore to be spent in FY27 if it starts.
Tower crane capacity is about 950-1,000 units a year versus about 680-690 units produced in FY26 (FY25 comparison not given).
demand_pricing: Tower crane order books are full; demand is strong into the start of Q1, with slowdown usually beginning mid-to-late June during monsoon.

Hydra-type cranes (about 60% of the market) shrank in FY26 on emission-norm skepticism and are recovering since January-February; management expects higher volumes in backhoe loaders and construction equipment.
Price realisation per unit rose on a mix shift to higher tonnage cranes; emission-transition costs added an estimated 5-7% to blended cost per unit.
About INR40-50 crore of Q4 revenue was lost to Middle East-bound export shipments stuck in India and March delivery deferrals.

Competition: Chinese players are absent from pick-and-carry cranes (below 30-35 tonnes) and compete in slew/heavy cranes (40-50+ tonnes), offering 1-2 year credit terms; competitor segment margins are about 8-9% versus about 18-19% for ACE.
Anti-dumping duties of 25-52% on Chinese cranes were recommended by DGTR in September 2025 but not notified by the Finance Ministry; the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Status of LD implementation and Chinese competition in pick-and-carry cranes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese players do not make pick-and-carry cranes; they compete in heavy slew cranes (40-50+ tonnes). The anti-dumping order was not notified, and the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-current investments large and what is their size?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash is invested in secured, listed bonds with 1-3 year tenures, classified as non-current under accounting rules but saleable; the amount is about INR700-750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR76.55 crore 'others' revenue and the impairment line?
qa_highlights.answer: 'Others' is miscellaneous exports, reported separately by the auditors. Impairment is a prudent expected-credit-loss provision on slightly delayed receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark-to-market losses on investments at March month-end; partly recovered in April. Management expects INR20-35 crore of other income in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes grow 10%+ in FY27 and what are price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 growth of 15-20% or more is possible on a low base; annual guidance is deferred to mid-Q2. Price hikes total 9-10% with another 3-4% possible, against 11-14% cost inflation (steel about 65% of cost, up 20-22% since January).

qa_highlights.question: What is the KATO JV revenue potential and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue of about INR300 crore in 3-4 years under current conditions, potentially INR700-800 crore if anti-dumping duties are imposed. Chinese imports are priced 25-30% below Indian-made costs, aided by credit terms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and tower crane factory timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR200 crore; a INR400 crore tower crane factory is need-based, with a 12-18 month build.

risks_watch: Steel (about 65% of cost) up 20-22% since January; the price pass-through lags 2-3 months and may not fully recover 11-14% inflation.
Anti-dumping duty notification remains pending; the outcome determines JV scale and Chinese pricing pressure.
Other income is volatile due to mark-to-market exposure on treasury investments (INR700-750 crore).
Demand is capital-goods-linked; management flagged geopolitical risk, rupee depreciation, and a possible monsoon slowdown from mid-June.
Other expenses are largely fixed, so margins are sensitive to volume shortfalls; volumes fell about 18-20% in FY26 (about 13,300 to 10,800 units by the analyst's count).
ROCE fell from about 40% to 32% over two years; capex timing is tied to demand before the tower crane factory is approved.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term demand and pricing power, but evasive on full-year numbers, which were deferred to mid-Q2 FY27 citing turbulence from the West Asia conflict. Management was candid about cost pressures and the lapsed anti-dumping order, and it framed margin protection as the first priority over market share.
key_quotes: Despite these geopolitical headwinds, we responded with agility and operational discipline to deliver our best ever revenue performance in quarter 4 last year with sustained operating margins to fortify our balance sheet.
Our focus remains on driving volume-led competitive growth with right balance on pricing.
So our competition at segment level, I think they are at 8%, 9% margin, whereas we are close to 18%, 19% margin.

adds.what: Proposed new tower crane factory (capex upwards of INR400 crore), on hold; decision need-based, ~INR150 crore spend in FY27 if started
New defense and new-product plant within existing complex (INR40-50 crore capex in FY27)

growth.why: Management guides Q1 FY27 growth of 15-20% and FY29 revenue of INR6,000-6,200 crore (about 1.8x FY26), backed by a ~INR575 crore order book, 9-10% price hikes, defense execution of INR200-220 crore and tower crane orders that are full, but utilisation is only ~60% and the INR400 crore tower crane plant is on hold, so long-term capacity backing is thin.
